text:
Noah: follow-up from RFC review: we need a clear contract for priority hints + fairness across tenants when ingest is overloaded. saw a case where one noisy client starved downstream processing.
Priya: can you summarize the noisy pattern? spikes, retries, or large bulk uploads?
Noah: mostly repeated retries from a mobile rollout + some background batch telemetry. retries amplified because clients didn't honor Retry-After.
Zoe: client misbehavior aside, server should enforce fairness. propose two levers: 1) per-tenant token-bucket with short leases, 2) global fairness window that enforces round-robin allocation across active tenants.
Santiago: round-robin across thousands of tenants could be expensive. maybe do weighted fair-queueing at an ingress shard level (per-shard tenant set). cheaper and still prevents single-tenant hogging.
Priya: agree on sharded WFQ. add an ingress hint for "priority: low|normal|high". low-priority can be dropped under pressure or compacted (coalesce metrics).
Noah: how do we define compaction semantics? e.g., aggregate counter metrics with same key in 1s window, drop raw spans for low priority?
Zoe: compaction rules: metrics -> sketch/rollup (1s), logs -> sample 1-in-N or drop body, spans -> keep only root & error spans for low-priority. documentable and opt-in per-tenant.
Santiago: implementation sketch for token leases:
```
ingest_shard:
  wfq:
    queue_slots: 1024
    lease_ttl_ms: 100
  tenant_bucket_default:
    rate_qps: "50"
    burst: "100"
  low_priority_compaction: true
```
Noah: lease_ttl 100ms seems reasonable to smooth refills and avoid herd. also emitting a metric when a lease is handed: tenant.leases_granted, tenant.leases_denied.
Priya: telemetry surface: per-tenant: ingest.tokens_used, ingest.tokens_denied, ingest.compacted_count; global: ingest.shard_congested, ingest.global_rejects, wfq.queue_depth. Also a histogram for retry_after_ms.
Zoe: tracing: add tags to dropped items: ingest.drop_reason=(compaction|low_priority|hard_reject), ingest.shard_id, ingest.tenant_window_pct.
Santiago: ops playbook: when shard_congested > 5% over 5m, check top 10 tenants by tokens_used. escalate if reserved_capacity tenant is causing it.
Noah: for Dedicated/reserved customers we need bypass paths: reserved tokens that are drawn from a separate pool per-tenant and only fall back to shared pool when reserved exhausted. still obey WFQ fairness across reserved pools to avoid single reserved tenant starving control plane.
Priya: security note: ensure reserved-token auth is validated at the edge and logged. Also rate-limits should be plumbed into quota billing so we can charge for reserved throughput.
Zoe: rollout plan: feature gate in staging with simulated noisy clients, then enable in 10% prod shards (canary), monitor ingest.shard_congested, error rates, and latency p50/p95.
Santiago: backwards compat: if client doesn't send priority hint, treat as normal. clients that aggressively retry despite Retry-After should be subject to exponential penalty: escalate from token denial -> 429 -> 503 on repeated violations.
ingest-bot: NOTE: staging config applied: wfq.enabled=true, lease_ttl_ms=100, low_priority_compaction=true
Noah: I'll open a small RFC PR with the compaction rules + metric names + shard WFQ plan. @Priya @Zoe @Santiago please review.
Priya: minor wording in PR: prefer metric name ingest.tokens_denied_total to follow prometheus convention.
Zoe: add a dashboard with per-shard top tenants and a heatmap of queue_depth. makes oncall troubleshooting faster.
Santiago: adding runbook steps: 1) identify shard, 2) list top tenants, 3) apply temporary throttle to tenant via admin API, 4) notify tenant owner.
Noah: thanks all. PR incoming. :rocket:
